faq.q: Why are the spots of light under a tree round?
faq.a: Each small gap between leaves works like a pinhole camera and projects an image of the Sun onto the ground. Since the Sun is round, the spots are round, whatever shape the gaps are.
asks: Why are the light patches under trees round?

faq.q: How does a pinhole camera work?
faq.a: Light travels in straight lines. Rays from each part of a bright object pass through a tiny hole and cross over, making an upside-down image on the surface behind.
asks: Why is a pinhole image upside down?

faq.q: Why do the spots become crescents in an eclipse?
faq.a: During a partial eclipse the Moon covers part of the Sun, leaving a crescent. Each leaf gap projects an image of that crescent Sun, so the ground fills with crescents.
asks: Why are there crescents under trees during an eclipse?
How can I see an eclipse safely?

faq.q: Why are some spots bigger than others?
faq.a: The size of a pinhole image depends on how far the gap is from the ground. Gaps high in the tree make bigger spots, about one hundred and eighth of their height across.
asks: Why are spots under tall trees bigger?
How big is a pinhole image of the Sun?

faq.q: Why are the spots oval on a slope?
faq.a: The light arrives at a slant on sloping ground, so each round image is stretched into an oval, just as a torch beam does when you shine it at an angle.
asks: Why are sun spots on the ground stretched?
Why are the light patches oval?

facts: A pinhole image of the Sun is about one hundred and eighth as wide as the distance from the hole to the screen, because the Sun appears about half a degree wide.
Writers in ancient China and Greece described pinhole images more than 2,000 years ago.

quiz.say: During a partial solar eclipse, what shape are the spots of light under a tree?
quiz.show: Under a tree during a partial eclipse, the light spots are…
quiz.why: Each gap projects an image of the Sun, and during a partial eclipse the Sun is a crescent.

wrong.0: The spots show the Sun's shape, not the gap's shape.
wrong.2: The spots change because the Sun itself has a bite taken out of it.
